Chapter 5: Making Decisive Choices and Embracing New Realities
So, after all the experimenting and learning that happens during a big turning point, there comes a moment when a choice has to be made.
You can’t stay in the exploration phase forever. At some point, leaders have to pick a direction, put resources behind it, and get everyone moving together on the same path.
And let’s be honest—these choices? They’re rarely simple. There’s usually a lot at stake, the risks can be huge, and you won’t always know how things will turn out.
Sometimes, the right move even means letting go of products, markets, or traditions that have defined the organization for years. That can be tough—sometimes even painful. But here’s the thing: holding on to the past? That’s often the biggest risk of all.
Making these big decisions starts with weighing all the evidence you’ve gathered during your experiments. You look at what your team does well, where you might struggle, and what’s happening out in the world. Then it takes courage—to act even when you don’t have every answer.
One way to think about this is like “betting the company.” The stakes are high. The choices you make now will shape the future for years ahead. That doesn’t mean you should act without thinking, but it does mean you have to be bold when the moment calls for it.
And once you’ve made that call, it’s time to bring everyone on board. That might mean shifting teams around, moving resources, or even redefining what certain roles look like. Most importantly, you’ve got to explain why this decision was made—so everyone understands the reasons and what’s expected of them moving forward.
Here are a few practical steps you can take to make strong decisions and embrace what’s next:
First, take a hard look at your options. Use real data from your experiments to judge which strategies have the most promise. And be honest about the risks and trade-offs involved.
Next, once you make a decision, commit to it. Put your energy and resources behind the new strategy. Try not to get caught up in second-guessing or wavering.
And finally, support your people as they adapt. Offer training, encouragement, and whatever help they need to get comfortable in new roles or ways of working.
When you make decisive choices and truly embrace new realities, you help your organization move past uncertainty. Suddenly, you’re not just reacting to change—you’re laying the groundwork for a whole new chapter of success.
